R150.note: IsPathRooted rejection plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment closes both the rooted-override and ..\ traversal; the StartsWith("..") test would also reject a file literally named "..x" inside the root, but that is a negligible edge.

R151.note: Encode.forHtml at the HTML-body sink is the right context encoder; the OWASP Java Encoder dependency is named though unversioned, and output is unchanged for benign names.

R152.note: Pinning token.Method to *jwt.SigningMethodRSA in the keyfunc is the documented golang-jwt pattern (jwt.WithValidMethods would be the equivalent v5 option); RS256/384/512 tokens still verify and nothing else changes.

R153.note: Decoding into a Command/Priority-only DTO keeps the gob wire format (gob ignores sender fields absent from the receiver) and IsAdmin is set server-side to false, which the write-up states; matches the contract.

R154.note: resolve-then-normalize with Path.startsWith(BASE_DIR) rejects absolute and ../ inputs before the read and throws IOException, which the signature already declares; in-base reports still return their bytes.

R155.note: The AST allowlist evaluator removes eval and rejects calls/attributes/unknown names as the contract requires, but it also adds a 1000-character expression cap (only a code comment mentions it, the explanation does not) that would reject a long legitimate formula the original accepted.

R156.note: text() with a :date_filter bind and a parameter dict on connection.execute is the correct SQLAlchemy Core shape; query semantics and result shape are unchanged.

R157.note: strnlen bounded by sizeof(record->name) never reads into flags and returns the existing length for NUL-terminated names; an unterminated name yields 16 (== sizeof), the conventional no-terminator sentinel the caller can test, which satisfies the contract.

R158.note: Single snprintf into message[64] with a >= sizeof truncation check rejects oversized input with -1 instead of overflowing or truncating, and fitting inputs still produce "AUDIT user:action" and return 0.

R159.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) closes object instantiation while keeping the wire format, so empty/invalid cookies and legitimate array carts behave exactly as before; note the contract's stronger wording (unsigned cookies not reaching unserialize at all, i.e. HMAC) is not implemented, so attacker bytes still hit the parser.

R160.note: Tika.detect on the bytes replaces trust in the client Content-Type and drives both the allowlist and the stored extension; the switch to Files.write with CREATE_NEW and the new tika-core dependency (unversioned) are both stated and block no legitimate upload, though the whole file is now buffered in memory.

R161.note: min(claimedCapacity, segment.size()) guarantees index < size so the write cannot leave the span and valid writes still land; the claimedCapacity parameter is retained rather than removed as the contract's last clause suggests, but it can no longer cause harm.

R162.note: ? placeholder with DB::select($sql, [$region]) is the correct Laravel binding shape; the query and JSON response are otherwise unchanged.

R163.note: createElement/textContent/createTextNode reproduce the same span+text structure with both untrusted values as text nodes, so no HTML is parsed and rendered output for plain chat text is identical.

R164.note: Build FAIL: JexlSandbox lives in org.apache.commons.jexl3.introspection, not org.apache.commons.jexl3, and there is no allow(Class, String...) overload; worse, new JexlSandbox(false) constructs a black-listing sandbox (everything allowed unless blocked), so even if it compiled the claimed deny-all posture is inverted and the engine stays unrestricted.

R165.note: min_val + secrets.randbelow(max_val - min_val + 1) is CSPRNG-backed and reproduces randint's inclusive range exactly, including raising ValueError when max < min as before.

R166.note: Checking frameBuffer.size() >= payloadLength before memcpy and returning false through the existing bool channel stops the over-read; successful extractions and lastPayloadSize_ behave as before.
